samasa.alt: दाव itself can mean ‘forest fire’; then a karmadhāraya, दावः एव अनलः. The ṣaṣṭhī reading, दाव = ‘forest’, is the usual one.

Nominative plural of the i-stem अरि with guṇa of the stem vowel: अरि → अरय् + अः.
Present second singular of परि + √पा ‘to protect’ (adādi: पा-सि); परि ‘all around’ strengthens the sense: ‘you guard on every side’.

mantras.anvaya: यत्र रक्षांसि, यत्र उग्रविषाः नागाः च, यत्र अरयः, यत्र दस्युबलानि, यत्र दावानलः, तथा अब्धिमध्ये, तत्र स्थिता त्वं विश्वं परिपासि।
mantras.anvaya_en: A series of relative clauses of place (यत्र …) with the verb ‘to be’ understood, closed by the correlative तत्र and the main clause.
mantras.lit: Where there are rākṣasas, where serpents of fierce venom, where enemies, where bands of robbers, where a forest fire, and likewise in the midst of the ocean — standing there, you protect the world.
mantras.tr: Where demons are, and serpents of deadly venom, where enemies and robber bands, where the forest is ablaze, and out on the open sea — there you stand and guard the world.

comm.t: A catalogue of the dangers of the wild and of travel: demons, snakes, enemies, robbers, fire, the sea. Wherever danger is, the Goddess is there (तत्र स्थिता) and protects. The repeated यत्र, four times in three lines, builds the list.

The Devī makes the matching promise in chapter 12: one who remembers her story is freed from distress when surrounded by forest fire, beset by robbers or held by enemies, or tossed by the wind ‘in a ship on the great ocean’ (12.25–29 दावाग्निपरिवारितः … दस्युभिर्वा वृतः … स्थितः पोते महार्णवे).
A modern reading: the hymn does not say she removes every danger from the world, but that she stands within it. Protection is presence.

samasa.alt: Also ‘she who is the self of the universe’ (विश्वस्य आत्मा यस्याः स्वरूपम्); the -आत्मिका formation allows both. The reason clause (इति) fits either: because she is one with it, she holds it.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (with the gerundive वन्द्य) containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (विश्वेश)
samasa.literal: to be revered by the lords of the universe
samasa.sense: honoured even by the gods who rule the world
a shelter for the whole world

morph.note: The honorific pronoun भवत् ‘Your Honour’ (feminine भवती) takes a third-person verb. It sits beside भवन्ति (√भू, 3 pl.): the same sound in two different words, a deliberate echo.
धारयति ‘holds, supports’ has the causative form but the sense of the simple root √धृ. With the preceding विश्वात्मिका … इति: ‘being the universe’s self, you uphold it’.
वन्द्य is the gerundive (ण्यत्) of √वन्द् (bhvādi 1Ā ‘to praise, revere’): ‘to be revered’.

mantras.anvaya: हे विश्वेश्वरि, त्वं विश्वं परिपासि। (त्वं) विश्वात्मिका (असि) इति विश्वं धारयसि। भवती विश्वेशवन्द्या (अस्ति)। ये त्वयि भक्तिनम्राः, (ते) विश्वाश्रयाः भवन्ति।
mantras.anvaya_en: Four short statements, one to a line: she protects; being its self she sustains; she is revered by its lords; her devotees become its refuge.
mantras.lit: O Queen of the universe, you protect the universe; being the self of the universe, therefore you uphold the universe. Your Ladyship is to be revered by the lords of the universe; those who are bowed in devotion to you become the refuges of the universe.
mantras.tr: Queen of the universe, you guard the universe; as its very self you hold the universe up. The lords of the universe revere you, and those who bow to you in devotion become the shelter of the universe.

comm.t: The word विश्व ‘universe’ is struck six times in four lines. She protects the universe, sustains it because it is her own self, is honoured by its rulers, and makes her devotees its refuge. The last line takes up 11.29: those who take refuge in her become a refuge (आश्रयतां प्रयान्ति).

The thought that she holds the world because she is its self is Brahmā’s in the first carita (1.75 त्वयैतद्धार्यते विश्वं), and the gods opened this hymn with the same title (11.3 प्रसीद विश्वेश्वरि पाहि विश्वम्). ‘The lords of the universe’ are the ruling gods, who, as Brahmā says, took their bodies through her (1.84–85).
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has विश्वधारिणी (name 759), ‘she who upholds the universe’. A shared idea; separate works.

samasa.sense: through your victory over Śumbha and his host

samasa.sense: the disasters that portents foretell, coming to fruition

morph.note: Imperative second singular of the curādi root √पाल् (stem पालय-), with परि ‘all around’: ‘protect on every side’. The stanza has three imperatives: प्रसीद, परिपालय, नय.
Imperative of √नी (thematic stem नय-). With the accusative of the goal प्रशमम्, ‘lead to quiescence’: an idiom for ‘put an end to’.
जनित, the last member, is the past participle of the causative of √जन् ‘to be born’: ‘brought to birth, produced’.

mantras.anvaya: हे देवि, प्रसीद। यथा अधुना एव असुरवधात् सद्यः (अस्मान् अपालयः), (तथा) नित्यं नः अरिभीतेः परिपालय। सर्वजगतां पापानि उत्पातपाकजनितान् महोपसर्गान् च आशु प्रशमं नय।
mantras.anvaya_en: Three imperatives. The second is qualified by a comparison (यथा … सद्यः) whose verb is understood; the third has two objects joined by च and the goal प्रशमम्.
mantras.lit: O Devī, be gracious; protect us always from the fear of enemies, as (you did) just now, at once, through the slaying of the asuras; lead quickly to extinction the sins of all the worlds and the great calamities born of the ripening of portents.
mantras.tr: Be gracious, Devī. Guard us always from fear of our foes, as you did just now, at once, by slaying the asuras. Swiftly bring to rest the sins of all the worlds and the great calamities that ripen from evil portents.
mantras.tr_note: ‘as you did’ supplies the verb implied by यथा; ‘our’ is supplied with ‘foes’.

comm.t: The last long stanza of the hymn, in vasantatilakā (fourteen syllables a line), the metre of the gods’ hymn in chapter 4, which also opened a stanza with देवि प्रसीद (4.14). The gods ask for continued protection, citing what she has just done, and for the calming of sin and calamity in every world.

The Devī herself promises the same in chapter 12: hearing her story ‘would quell all calamities born of plague, and the threefold portent’ (12.8 उपसर्गानशेषांस्तु महामारीसमुद्भवान्। तथा त्रिविधमुत्पातं माहात्म्यं शमयेन्मम), and she prescribes its hearing in every rite of pacification (12.16–17). The prayer of chapter 11 and the promise of chapter 12 answer each other.
A modern reading: ‘as you did just now’ — the prayer rests on remembered help. Gratitude for the past becomes trust for the future.

samasa.vigraha: विश्वस्य आर्तिः विश्वार्तिः; विश्वार्तिं हरति इति विश्वार्तिहारिणी, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (हारिन् = √हृ with the agent affix -इन्, feminine -ई) containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (विश्वार्ति)
samasa.literal: she who takes away the affliction of the world

samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (वासिन् = √वस् with the agent affix -इन्)
samasa.literal: of those who dwell in the three worlds

samasa.sense: she who grants what is asked

morph.note: Gerundive of √ईड् ‘to praise’: ईड्य ‘to be praised’, feminine ईड्या, vocative ईड्ये. With a gerundive the agent may stand in the genitive (त्रैलोक्यवासिनाम् ‘by the dwellers of the three worlds’).
Genitive plural of the past participle प्रणत ‘bowed down’ (the n of √नम् becomes ṇ after the r of the prefix प्र). प्रसीद takes the genitive of the person favoured: ‘be gracious to those who bow’.
त्रैलोक्य ‘the three worlds’ is a taddhita (with vṛddhi of the first vowel) from त्रिलोक; वासिन् ‘dweller’ is an agent noun of √वस् ‘to dwell’.

mantras.anvaya: हे विश्वार्तिहारिणि त्रैलोक्यवासिनाम् ईड्ये देवि, त्वं प्रणतानां प्रसीद, लोकानां वरदा भव।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two imperatives addressed to one subject (त्वम्), each with a genitive of the persons concerned (प्रणतानाम्, लोकानाम्); three vocatives name her.
mantras.lit: Be gracious, you, to those who bow down, O Devī, remover of the world’s affliction; O you who are to be praised by the dwellers of the three worlds, be the giver of boons to the worlds.
mantras.tr: Be gracious to those who bow before you, Devī, who take away the sorrow of the world. Praised by all who dwell in the three worlds, be the giver of boons to all the worlds.

comm.t: The last verse of the gods’ hymn (the Nārāyaṇī Stuti, 11.3–35) returns to the anuṣṭubh and closes with a request: ‘be the giver of boons’ (वरदा भव). The Devī answers at once in the next verses with the same word: वरदाहं सुरगणा वरं यन्मनसेच्छथ (11.37), ‘I am the giver of boons, hosts of gods; choose the boon you wish’.

The hymn is framed by one prayer. It opened with देवि प्रपन्नार्तिहरे प्रसीद (11.3), ‘O Devī who remove the affliction of those who take refuge, be gracious’, and it ends with प्रसीद … विश्वार्तिहारिणि: the remover of the suppliants’ pain is now the remover of the world’s.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the name वरदा (name 331). A shared epithet; separate works.
